day.adaptation: the household's labelled windows closing within 1 days of its first observation
day.scored: its labelled windows closing after that

week.adaptation: the household's labelled windows closing within 7 days of its first observation
week.scored: its labelled windows closing after that

calibration: expected calibration error over 10 confidence bins

criteria.does not overfit: log loss is negligible or favours the unconstrained model
criteria.overfits: log loss favours the pooled model over the unconstrained one
criteria.pooling_failure: log loss is negligible or favours the reference
criteria.pooling_success: log loss favours the adapted model, and neither balanced accuracy nor calibration error favours the reference
criteria.pooling_trade-off: log loss favours the adapted model and balanced accuracy favours the reference
criteria.primary: P1 and P2 answer whether pooling helps; O1 whether unconstrained fitting overfits small homes; the others are read by the same rules
criteria.verdicts: favours model: mean >= delta and lower bound > 0; favours reference: mean <= -delta and upper bound < 0; negligible: the whole interval within (-delta, delta); uncertain: anything else
criteria.why_log_loss: adaptation changes each household's probability model, so a proper scoring rule is the target; balanced accuracy and calibration error are guards

eligibility.cells: a channel and state with no household windows takes the population value in every adapted model
eligibility.rule: a household enters an arm's comparisons with at least min_adaptation_windows labelled windows in its adaptation window and min_scored_windows labelled windows after it; otherwise it is reported and left out of every model in that arm

estimands.question: does partial pooling improve on the population, current windows
does partial pooling improve on the population, the recursion
does unconstrained per-home fitting overfit small homes: pooled against unconstrained after one day
the same after one day, the recursion
does a strength selected on training households improve on the population, current windows
does partial pooling improve on the population after one day
does unconstrained per-home fitting improve on the population after one week
the population fit against the declared rates, current windows

households.use: each household is held out once; its fold's training households fit the population and select the pooling strength

inference: online filter: I0 and R read no window after the scored one

declared.emissions: default_emissions of the household registry, pooled per channel
declared.fitted: nothing: every parameter is the declared default
declared.prediction: most probable state of the posterior; no abstention
declared.prior: stationary distribution of the default ontology, one step before the first declared window
declared.transition: default StateOntology, time-homogeneous, one step per window
declared.windows: the set's current window, plus its lagged windows with recent history

pooled.channels: hurdle, the household pooled toward the population

pooled_selected.channels: hurdle, the household pooled toward the population with the strength selected on the fold's training households

population.channels: hurdle, fitted per fold on the training households as in the Phase 3.3 follow-up
population.emissions: default_emissions of the household registry, pooled per channel
population.fitted: nothing: every parameter is the declared default
population.prediction: most probable state of the posterior; no abstention
population.prior: stationary distribution of the default ontology, one step before the first declared window
population.transition: default StateOntology, time-homogeneous, one step per window
population.windows: the set's current window, plus its lagged windows with recent history

unconstrained.why: half a window keeps a probability off 0 and 1; with a few windows the household's own data dominate, and a cell without any takes the population value

name: phase3-partial-pooling

per_state_recall.rare_rule: share of labelled time below 0.05 in either fold's training households

pooling.estimator: theta_pop + w (theta_raw - theta_pop), w = n / (n + kappa), for the silence probability and the active-window mean of every channel and state
pooling.why: 288 windows is 24 labelled hours, the framework's default and the Phase 3.1 household pooling strength

selection.choice: the smallest mean log loss; a tie goes to the larger strength
selection.held_out: the fold's held-out households are never used
selection.procedure: for each fold, leave one training household out at a time: fit the population on the other training households, pool the left-out household with its week-arm window, score its labelled windows after the window in I0, and take the mean log loss over the eligible training households

settings.R: the filter's recursion fed every window of the recording from the stationary distribution

stratification: within each arm, eligible households are sorted by labelled adaptation windows (ties by name); the first half is 'less data', the rest 'more data'; every estimand is also reported within each stratum
tuning: none on held-out households: the strength is declared, or selected on training households only
